ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, and UBOs against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act (SC 1992, c. 17), the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (SC 2011, c. 17), and the Terrorist Financing Freeze Regulations. Enhanced risk-based KYC review required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) under the FINTRAC regulatory framework.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Name Reservation and NUANS Search System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French script, with mandatory transliteration of any non-Latin characters into romanized form. Alberta does not permit purely symbolic, numeric, or pictorial names unless accompanied by a legal element. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names and comply with the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) and NUANS search requirements.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Registrar under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), specifically requesting a re-review of the NUANS report and submitting legal argument that the proposed name is not confusingly similar. Such appeal must be submitted in writing within 30 calendar days of the rejection notice, supported by evidence of prior market presence, trademark registrations, or consent letters from existing name holders.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual registered office is generally permissible for the IT software industry provided the entity maintains a physical director/agent address within Alberta. The virtual office must be able to accept service of process during normal business hours. Registration of the remote screen-share and IoT business will not be refused solely for using a virtual office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, being Alberta’s primary corporate statute, together with the Alberta Corporate Registry Regulation and corporation naming rules under that Act
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under Alberta law. The articles may authorize an unconditional share structure with no stated par value; no escrow account, capital deposit, or paid-up capital threshold applies, including for non-resident shareholders. Allocation of subscription consideration is fixed by the board of directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that: 1. The subscriptions to the corporation, as set out in the subscription schedule accompanying these minutes, are accepted, and the corresponding shares are issued as fully paid on the consideration approved by the board. 2. The registered office located at [Alberta street address], as stated in the Notice of Registered Office, is adopted and maintained as the corporation’s registered office and records address. 3. The following individuals are appointed to the offices set beside their names: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, each to hold office until removed by resolution of the board. 4. The board accepts the initial by-laws, authorizes banking resolutions, and directs officers to implement all required filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via an accredited Corporate Registry service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name to an approved service provider for a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report. Confirm the name is distinguishable from existing Alberta and extra-provincial registrations and does not contain restricted words without authorization. Retain the report for attachment to the incorporation application. Notarization is not required at this stage.
required_dossiers: Signed instruction letter to service provider
Proposed corporate name and alternative names, if any
Incorporator contact and jurisdiction details
Payment authorization for NUANS and service provider fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a conflicting name is identified, select the first available alternative from the submitted list, or file a written request for consent when the proposed name contains regulated terminology.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation, Registered Office Notice, and Initial Directors’ Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and the first board of directors; notarization is required only when third parties or foreign process agents demand commissioned signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the ABCA Form 1 Articles of Incorporation together with the Notice of Registered Office and the Notice of Directors. The registered office must be a real and fully locatable Alberta street address, not a post-office box. The named directors must meet statutory capacity and residency requirements for Alberta corporations. Sign the articles and have each signature witnessed in accordance with the form instructions.
required_dossiers: Executed ABCA Form 1 Articles of Incorporation
Notice of Registered Office with Alberta municipal street address
Notice of Directors with names, residential addresses, and Canadian residency status
NUANS name search report
Incorporator identification documents if notarization is obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry identifies an incomplete signature, invalid registered-office description, or director ineligibility, the incorporators shall execute a corrective schedule or revised form within the registry’s permitted correction window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Alberta Corporate Registry and Payment of Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Registrar of Corporations, through licensed Corporate Registry access providers or in-person registry counter service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically file the executed Articles and initial notices through the approved service-provider portal or deliver them to the corporate registry counter. Pay the Alberta incorporation fee and any service-provider fees. Upon validation, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation reflecting the Alberta corporation number and incorporation date.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation in electronic PDF or scanned form
NUANS name search report
Notice of Registered Office
Notice of Directors
Proof of fee payment or service provider confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for missing information, fee insufficiency, or name confusion, file a corrected or substituted application within the registry’s resubmission period; any paid fee is applied to the corrected filing at the Registrar’s discretion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organization Meeting of the Board, Adoption of By-laws, and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First board of directors acting as the corporation’s governing organ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issue of the Certificate of Incorporation, hold the first directors’ meeting or pass a unanimous written consent resolution. Adopt the initial by-laws; ratify the issuance of shares to the subscribing incorporators; confirm the registered office; appoint officers; approve the corporate seal and bank signatory authorities; and authorize the opening of a corporate bank account.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Pro-forma first board resolution or written consent resolution
Subscription schedule and share certificates
Initial by-laws
Officer acknowledgements and consent forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed officer or director cannot act, the board shall appoint a replacement by written consent or at a properly convened directors’ meeting, updating the corporate records accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Records Register, Registered Office Records Deposit, and Annual Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors, the corporate secretary, or designated authorized agent of the corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create and maintain the statutory minute book including the share register, directors’ register, officers’ register, significant-individual/beneficial-ownership register where applicable, and registered-office records address. Confirm that the Alberta registered office location is accessible for service and records inspection. Set a compliance calendar for the annual return to the Alberta Corporate Registry and any municipal business licence renewal.
required_dossiers: Corporate minute book and share certificate book
Registered office address confirmation, including lease or owner’s consent if applicable
Directors and officers register
Beneficial ownership or significant-individual register, as applicable
Annual return compliance calendar and registry reminder record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a corporate record or registered office address is found defective, the secretary shall amend the affected register, file a Notice of Change of Registered Office or Directors where required, and ensure record continuity within the statutory filing period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 remote desktop application, unattended machine telemetry, and screen-share software publishing is not an industrial or manufacturing activity subject to Alberta industrial licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — no provincial operating or manufacturing permit is required for remote-support software; a municipal business licence may be required only if a physical commercial office is opened in Alberta.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity involves no construction of major industrial infrastructure, no process discharge and no physical manufacturing, so no EIA registration or approval is triggered under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000 c E-3.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No direct statutory wastewater, VOC, or atmospheric discharge thresholds apply. If office premises are used, waste handling, electronic waste recycling, and municipal sewer discharge must comply with the Alberta Waste Control Regulation and applicable municipal bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000 c O-2, and Alberta Building Code fire safety requirements apply to any leased office space. Where employees work remotely from homes, a workplace hazard assessment is still required, and any dedicated office area must maintain fire egress, smoke alarms, and fire extinguishers as prescribed by the Alberta Fire Code and the local authority having jurisdiction.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). Primary portals are Business Registration Online (BRO), My Business Account, and Represent a Client. Alberta corporate income tax is administered through the CRA under federal-provincial tax administration arrangements; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance legislates Alberta corporate tax rates. Alberta has no general provincial sales tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate or register the entity federally or through the Alberta Corporate Registry and obtain the certificate of incorporation or registration. 2. Apply to the CRA for a nine-digit Business Number (BN) through Business Registration Online, Form RC1, or the applicable non-resident registration process. A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada generally requires a BN and a corporate income tax program account. 3. Register the corporation for the T2 corporation income tax account, where required, and obtain any applicable payroll, import-export, or information-return program accounts. 4. Register for GST/HST through BRO or CRA-authorized channels when registration is mandatory or voluntarily elected. The GST/HST program account is generally identified by the BN followed by the RT program suffix. 5. Authorize representatives and activate CRA online access where available. 6. Maintain the CRA legal name, registered office, directors, fiscal period, books and records, and beneficial ownership information consistently with corporate registry records. A foreign entity does not obtain an Alberta sales tax number because Alberta has no general retail sales tax; separate Alberta corporate registry, licensing, payroll, or municipal registrations may nevertheless apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Canadian corporation is generally taxed as a separate legal person and has no United States-style check-the-box election to elect partnership or disregarded-entity treatment. Canadian-resident corporations are generally taxable on worldwide income, subject to foreign tax relief and applicable treaty rules. Partnerships are ordinarily flow-through structures, but a corporation cannot unilaterally elect partnership treatment. Certain statutory elections can affect transactions or tax attributes, including corporate rollover elections under section 85 of the Income Tax Act, but these are not entity-classification elections. Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules may deny deductions or impose income inclusions for specified deduction or inclusion mismatches; they do not provide a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), with Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) applying in participating provinces. Alberta applies the federal GST only and does not impose a general provincial sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, determined under the small-supplier rules, generally measured over the relevant single-quarter and four-consecutive-quarter periods. The threshold is generally CAD 50,000 for public service bodies. Registration may be voluntary below the threshold. A corporation making taxable supplies in Canada, including taxable software or support services, must assess whether it is carrying on business in Canada and whether the small-supplier threshold is exceeded. Special simplified GST/HST rules may apply to non-resident vendors supplying digital products or services to Canadian consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general real-time GST invoice-clearance, mandatory continuous transaction control, or universal digital-stamping requirement for ordinary commercial supplies. GST registrants must issue prescribed documentation when required, retain electronic or paper books and records, and maintain records that permit verification of tax charged, input tax credits, place of supply, customer status, and zero-rating. Electronic invoices are generally acceptable if they preserve authenticity, integrity, readability, auditability, and required invoice particulars. CRA may require electronic filing for specified returns or information filings, but this is not equivalent to real-time invoice clearance. Import and export customs data may be filed electronically through the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), including the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) where applicable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST zero-rating is transaction-specific and is not available merely because a supplier receives foreign currency or because software is delivered online. Exported goods may generally be zero-rated when they are supplied for export and the statutory export, delivery, and documentary conditions are satisfied. Services supplied to a non-resident may generally be zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident and the service is not excluded by the Excise Tax Act, including exclusions for certain services connected with Canadian real property, tangible personal property, or litigation and other Canadian activities. Certain supplies of intangible personal property, software rights, electronically supplied services, and remote support services may qualify where the statutory non-resident and use or connection conditions are met. The supplier should verify the customer’s non-resident status, GST/HST registration status where relevant, contractual recipient, place of use, service performance, and applicable exclusions. Services supplied to a Canadian customer, or services effectively consumed or used in Canada, are generally taxable at the applicable GST/HST rate. A registrant claiming zero-rating must retain contracts, invoices, customer representations, delivery or access records, payment evidence, and records supporting the statutory place-of-supply analysis.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For exported physical goods where reporting is required: CBSA export declaration filed through CERS or the applicable permitted reporting method
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, purchaser, description, quantity, value, currency, and delivery terms
Bill of lading, airway bill, courier record, or other transportation document evidencing export from Canada
Proof of delivery or importation in the destination jurisdiction where relevant
Sales contract, purchase order, customer non-resident declaration, and evidence that the recipient is outside Canada or is otherwise eligible under the applicable zero-rating rule
Payment and accounting records, including bank settlement evidence where relevant; an inward remittance certificate is not a general Canadian statutory requirement

For remote software, cloud access, telemetry, or support services without physical goods: service agreement, customer location and status evidence, access or delivery logs, invoices, usage records, and evidence supporting the statutory zero-rating provision; a customs export declaration is generally not required for the electronic service itself
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days or within another fixed period solely to preserve GST zero-rating. CRA may reassess GST where zero-rating was unsupported, the recipient was not eligible, the supply was consumed in Canada, required export evidence was absent, or the transaction was mischaracterized. The reassessment can include GST collectible, denial or recovery of related input tax credits or refunds, arrears interest, and applicable administrative penalties. False statements or omissions may attract a penalty based on the applicable GST/HST penalty provisions, including gross-negligence penalties where the statutory conditions are met; deliberate fraud can result in prosecution under tax legislation. Physical-goods export reporting failures may also trigger CBSA administrative monetary penalties, seizure or other customs remedies. A refund or input tax credit obtained on the basis of an invalid zero-rating claim is recoverable through reassessment, interest, and penalties, subject to statutory limitation periods and extended periods for misrepresentation or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary and systemic authority; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises banks, while the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers cross-border fund reporting obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada maintains no dedicated foreign exchange control administration comparable to a SAFE-type authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada adheres fully to IMF Article VIII obligations, granting unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility. The Canadian dollar floats freely on international markets, and profit remittances of dividends, branch profits, interest, and royalties to non-residents require no central bank approval. The sole fiscal friction is Part XIII of the Income Tax Act: a 25% statutory withholding tax on passive payments, reduced to 5%-15% under Canada's tax treaties, and, for certain surplus-stripping scenarios, the application of thin-capitalization and earnings-stripping rules. Foreign-currency accounts may be held domestically and funded without convertibility quotas, exchange licenses, or prior authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds, no statutory conversion timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio for foreign-currency receivables. Software subscription receipts from remote-support and telemetry services may be retained in USD, EUR, or any convertible currency and either repatriated or held offshore at the corporation's discretion pending treasury policy. The only compulsory compliance duty is FINTRAC's electronic funds transfer report (ETR) for any cross-border wire transfer of CAD 10,000 or more in a single transaction day, together with standard record-keeping and client-identification obligations under the PCMLTFR.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with integrated merchant treasury services
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account plus USD clearing corridor

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ancillary treasury functions, Low for a primary operating account. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Wise, Revolut Business) may serve a Canadian corporation only as FINTRAC-registered money service businesses (MSBs) or unlicensed payment facilitators; they cannot lawfully take deposits in Canada under section 545 of the Bank Act, and their balances are not CDIC-insured. A compliant architecture uses a Tier-1 chartered bank as the settlement spine, with an offshore EMI wallet permitted solely for low-value FX isolation and contractor disbursement, swept daily to the domestic operating account to avoid regulatory and counterparty concentration risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate: the PCMLTFR permits remote identity verification only through a certified notarial package or an accredited digital identity credential, but in practice Alberta chartered banks require at least one director or a 25%+ ultimate beneficial owner to complete either an in-person branch interview or a bank-approved live video Conference call with notarized copies of foreign passports and proof-of-residence documents. The Alberta Business Corporations Act distinctly mandates a registered office in Alberta and at least one Canadian-resident director, which practically reinforces the need for a verifiable in-country nexus during onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: nominee shareholders, discretionary trust holdings, or a multi-tier foreign parent chain obscuring ultimate control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Alberta Corporate Registry extract and federal Corporations Canada filing; an organizational chart disclosing all UBOs at the 25%+ threshold; a beneficial-ownership attestation signed by each director; certified passport copies; and a share-issuance ledger evidencing the capitalization event.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus: inbound subscriber payments originating from FATF grey-listed or sanctioned states, or outbound disbursements to subcontractors in restricted corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP-address geolocation logs and session metadata from the remote-screen-share telemetry platform proving genuine end-user locations; executed customer and supplier contracts containing sanctioned-party exclusion warranties; a written export-control and sanctions-compliance policy; and SWIFT MT103 originator/beneficiary field data verifying transparent remittance chains.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-profile mismatch: high-frequency, low-value software subscriptions that diverge materially from the declared ISIC 6201 activity or initial turnover projections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Read-only access to Stripe and Paddle merchant dashboards demonstrating reconcilable subscription and invoicing flows; product documentation for the remote-support and IoT telemetry software; accountant-reviewed financial statements; and a platform-settlement reconciliation schedule matching expected vs. actual cleared volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital injection into the newly incorporated Alberta entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder funds-contribution agreement; the subscribing shareholder's bank statement evidencing the source of remitted funds; a board resolution authorizing the contribution; a directors' declaration of contributed surplus; and, where relevant, a CRA corporate profile or tax acknowledgment confirming the share issuance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border director/UBO identity inconsistency: multiple foreign-resident directors whose documentation lacks machine-readable uniformity or apostille certification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of passports and residency permits; Hague Convention apostilles for notarial certificates; a prime-bank reference letter issued in the director's home jurisdiction; and a completed FINTRAC-aligned risk questionnaire confirming non-PEP status, clean sanctions screening, and no adverse media.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital is routed via SWIFT MT103 from the subscribing shareholder's foreign bank to the Alberta corporation's Tier-1 settlement account; the sender must populate the purpose narrative with 'Share capital contribution - Board Resolution No. [X]' and use the receiving bank's designated capital-subscription payment code (commonly 'CAP' or 'INV'). The receiving bank screens the transfer against OFAC and OSFI sanctions lists and files a FINTRAC ETR for amounts of CAD 10,000 or more. Verification collateral includes the subscription agreement, the directors' capital-contribution resolution, the UBO attestation, and a statement of account reflecting the funds as unencumbered contributed surplus. Structuring the payment into multiple sub-threshold tranches to evade reporting is a criminal offence and will trigger immediate account suspension.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements for licensing, subcontractor payments, and cloud-infrastructure procurement settle by SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary BIC, account number, and USD ABA or EUR IBAN, using charge code OUR or SHA under the corporate banking fee template. Domestic CAD clearing rides the Lynx RTGS system (successor to LVTS) and the Real-Time Rail (RTR) for instant low-value claims. High-value cross-border physical or software trade settlements may use a commercial letter of credit confirmed by a Tier-1 Canadian bank, although MT103 is preferred for recurring telemetry-software subscriptions. Every outbound EFT of CAD 10,000 or more must be recorded in a FINTRAC ETR and screened against OSFI and OFAC sanctions lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Outright FX Forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) with tenors to 12 months under an ISDA/CSA master agreement
FX Swaps (simultaneous spot-forward exchange of principal and interest streams in two currencies)
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps for long-term foreign-currency receivables or debt service
Vanilla OTC FX Options (European-style CAD calls/puts) written by Schedule I banks
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) - legally permissible but commercially non-standard because CAD is fully deliverable; utilized only where a counterparty requires settlement in a restricted currency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date of incorporation, annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 30% of the fee; failure to file within 1 year of the anniversary date may result in administrative dissolution/strike-off by the Registrar

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporation Income Tax Return (Alberta Corporate Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Alberta Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31st day after the corporation's fiscal year-end; if no tax payable, still required for nil assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in a penalty of 5% of unpaid tax, plus 3% if late filing repeats; interest accrues daily on unpaid amounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (if permanent establishment in Alberta or deemed resident)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end, unless statute-extended to 12 months for non-resident corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty (5% of balance owing plus 3% for repeated failure); ministry may assess and collect; potential director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Filing (if registrant; standard annual regime)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end for fiscal-year-end filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 5%-10% of unpaid amounts plus interest at CRA prescribed rates; risk of accounts frozen

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Registered Office Information Update (if different from incorporation but generally part of annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must update within 60 days of any change, but annual attestation occurs with the annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct annual fee, but failure to update may lead to Notice of Change being required; recurring non-compliance can trigger strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Canada Business Corporations Act (for federal corporations) and Alberta Business Corporations Act, an audit is required for a corporation with gross revenues exceeding C$1,000,000 or assets exceeding C$1,000,000 at the end of the fiscal year, unless shareholders unanimously waive the audit (for provincially incorporated corporations under Alberta law)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) as adopted in Canada for public enterprises; for private business corporations, ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is deemed appropriate

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta corporations must file an annual return confirming the registered office, current directors, and any share-transfer-induced changes to the individual controlling the corporation. Alberta has no separate public UBO register; however, the corporation must maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISC) and confirm it annually to the board; failure to update may result in a fine of up to C$5,000
